translations.en: And from Abu Ibrahim al-Kazim (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: مَنْ فَرَّجَ عَنْ أَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ كُرْبَةً فَرَّجَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ كُرْبَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ.

translations.en: One who relieves his Muslim brother of a distress, Allah will relieve him of a distress on the Day of Resurrection.

en.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) highlights the reciprocal nature of divine mercy, where relieving a fellow believer's worldly distress serves as a prelude to relief from the ultimate tribulations of the Hereafter. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Mumin*, underscores the concept of *mu'akhat* (brotherhood) as a tangible mechanism for spiritual elevation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on active social responsibility as an extension of faith. The promise of alleviation on the Day of Judgment connects personal acts of kindness to the cosmic justice that defines the eschatological narrative.
en.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a Muslim brother in distress?
